malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware delivered via Facebook links, executed upon user download and launch.
malicious_snippets.code_language: varies (not specified, likely Windows PE, Android APK, or script)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code executes after the user downloads and opens a file from a Facebook link, performing malicious actions such as data theft or system compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Files delivered via social engineering on Facebook pages, with political lures, are a common malware delivery vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Facebook content should not deliver executable files or prompt users to download and run software.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software updates or downloads from official pages.
key_indicators: Executable files delivered via social media links
Use of political lures to increase click-through

execution_context.file_location: malicious ISO disk image attached to email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ISO file containing LokiBot or NanoCore binary, executed when user opens the ISO and runs the binary.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the user opens the ISO attachment, launches the embedded binary, which then steals credentials or provides remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: ISO attachments are rarely used for legitimate business email, and contain malware binaries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate ISO files should not be delivered via email or contain credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software distribution via ISO for legitimate software.

execution_context.file_location: virtual machine image launched by malicious installer

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Installer launches a Linux VM containing pre-installed cryptominer, which starts mining upon VM boot.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the installer launches a VM with a pre-configured cryptominer, which uses system resources to mine cryptocurrency for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected virtualization and cryptomining activity on user systems.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers should not launch hidden VMs or mine cryptocurrency.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of VMs for sandboxing or development.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware wipes storage, firewall rules, and network configuration, then halts the system.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware erases device storage, deletes firewall and network settings, and then stops the device, rendering it unusable.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Destructive actions targeting device availability and configuration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Firmware should not self-destruct or erase device configuration.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware records audio, takes over camera, and exfiltrates data.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app records audio, captures images/video, and sends the data to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited access to microphone and camera, and exfiltration of sensitive data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should not secretly record or exfiltrate user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use in video conferencing or voice recording apps (with user consent).

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Regin spyware payload targeting authentication systems.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the spyware attempts to compromise authentication systems and exfiltrate sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Highly targeted attack on authentication infrastructure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate software should attempt to subvert authentication systems.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Dridex banking trojan with new evasion techniques.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the trojan steals banking credentials and attempts to evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Banking trojans delivered via phishing are a common and dangerous threat.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Email attachments should not contain credential-stealing malware.

attack_chain.action: Victim is lured via social engineering (Facebook, email, app store, etc.)
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious file or app is downloaded or opened

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes on victim system (desktop, mobile, IoT, etc.)
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware performs its payload (data theft, cryptomining, device bricking, espionage, etc.)

attack_chain.action: Malware exfiltrates data, mines cryptocurrency, or destroys device functionality
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains profit, access, or causes disruption

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network connections from social media-linked files
Execution of binaries from ISO email attachments
Silent deployment of virtual machines with cryptomining activity
Mass deletion of system/network configuration files on IoT devices
Background audio/video recording and exfiltration on Android
Credential theft and evasion techniques in banking trojans
file_indicators: Unexpected VM images or virtualization software
Unusual firmware modifications on IoT devices
Phishing email attachments with executable payloads
network_indicators: Connections to known C2 infrastructure (for LokiBot, NanoCore, Dridex, Regin, etc.)
Outbound connections from IoT devices to unknown IPs
Data exfiltration endpoints for Android spyware
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of files delivered via social media or email, especially ISO attachments and repackaged APKs. Detect unexpected VM launches and cryptomining activity. Watch for mass file deletions or configuration wipes on IoT devices. Flag apps with excessive permissions and background recording on Android. Use threat intelligence to block known C2 domains and IPs associated with these malware families.
